_notes: Drug-disease and drug-syndrome entries from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria (Table 3, and Table 6 for the kidney-function entry). Each entry was checked against the published table on the date in its `verifiedOn` field; see docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md. This is a partial list and the wording is paraphrased. Drugs whose name alone cannot separate a flagged form from an unflagged one were left out on purpose. An absent flag does not mean a medication is safe. Not medical advice. An entry may carry `alsoShowFor`: other conditions under which the flag is still shown, each with a `qualifier` sentence that tells the user when it applies.

sources: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. Full text read from PubMed Central (author manuscript): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12478568/
NLM RxNorm and RxClass (https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/) for brand-name ingredients and for membership of classes the paper names without listing drugs.
verification.rule: Matchers ignore any entry whose `verified` value is not "confirmed" or "corrected".

sources.beers-2023-table-3: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. Table 3.
sources.beers-2023-table-6: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. Table 6.

entries.reason: These medicines block dopamine receptors and can worsen Parkinson disease symptoms.
entries.recommendation: Avoid.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Parkinson disease" (antiemetics); brand names checked in RxNorm

entries.reason: Antipsychotics block dopamine receptors and can worsen Parkinson disease symptoms. Quetiapine, clozapine and pimavanserin are exceptions and are not flagged.
entries.recommendation: Avoid.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Parkinson disease" (antipsychotics except clozapine, pimavanserin and quetiapine)
entries.verificationNote: The exception wording matches the table. The class list it uses was corrected (thioridazine removed).

entries.reason: May increase the risk of death in older adults with heart failure.
entries.recommendation: Avoid.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Heart failure" (cilostazol: avoid); brand names checked in RxNorm
entries.verificationNote: Reason corrected: the table ties cilostazol to increased mortality in heart failure, not to fluid retention.

alsoShowFor.qualifier: Applies if your heart failure has reduced ejection fraction - ask your doctor.

entries.reason: May promote fluid retention and worsen heart failure.
entries.recommendation: Avoid in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Heart failure" (nondihydropyridine CCBs: "Avoid in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction")
entries.verificationNote: The table says "Avoid in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction". The entry now belongs to the reduced-ejection-fraction condition and is a normal flag there. For someone who selected only general heart failure it is still shown, with the qualifier in `alsoShowFor`, so it is not silently dropped. Earlier corrections: the reason now gives the table's rationale, and an inferred sentence about preserved ejection fraction was removed (docs/RECHECK.md).

entries.recommendation: Avoid chronic use or persistent as-needed use. Avoid for behavioral problems of dementia unless non-drug options have failed or are not possible and the person is threatening substantial harm to self or others.

entries.reason: Can bring on or worsen delirium.
entries.recommendation: Avoid in people with delirium or at high risk of it. If needed, use the lowest dose for the shortest time and watch for delirium. Applies to oral and injected corticosteroids, not inhaled or topical forms.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Delirium" (corticosteroids, oral and parenteral) and footnote d; prednisone and methylprednisolone are corticosteroids in RxClass (ATC / FDA Established Pharmacologic Class); brand names checked in RxNorm
entries.verificationNote: Added the footnote's exclusion of inhaled and topical forms to the recommendation. The table lists corticosteroids under delirium only, not under dementia. It names the class without listing drugs.

entries.reason: May worsen existing ulcers or cause new ones.
entries.recommendation: Avoid unless other options are not effective and a stomach-protecting medicine can be taken.

entries.reason: May increase the risk of acute kidney injury and further loss of kidney function.
entries.recommendation: Avoid when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 6, row "NSAIDs (non-selective, COX-2 selective, and nonacetylated salicylates, oral and parenteral)" and footnote a
entries.verificationNote: This criterion is not in Table 3 of the 2023 paper: Table 10 records that it moved to Table 6. The threshold in the paper is creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min, not a CKD stage. Source string and recommendation corrected to say so.

entries.reason: May decrease urine flow and cause urinary retention.
entries.recommendation: Avoid in men. Antimuscarinic medicines prescribed for urinary incontinence are an exception and are not flagged.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Lower urinary tract symptoms, benign prostatic hyperplasia" (avoid in men; except antimuscarinics for urinary incontinence)

entries.reason: Can make urinary incontinence worse.
entries.recommendation: Avoid in women.

entries.verificationNote: The table row also lists oral and transdermal estrogen, which this entry leaves out.

entries.reason: Concerns about QT prolongation.
entries.recommendation: Avoid.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Heart failure" (dextromethorphan-quinidine: avoid); brand names checked in RxNorm
entries.verificationNote: Added in the follow-up from the gaps listed in section 6 of docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md. No qualifier in the row. It is the combination product, so a match needs both drug names together or the brand; dextromethorphan alone (cough medicine) and quinidine alone are not flagged. The alias with "hydrobromide" covers the way the generic product is labelled and is this file's own wording.

entries.reason: Can bring on or worsen delirium. Emerging data highlight an association between opioid use and delirium.
entries.recommendation: Avoid in people with delirium or at high risk of it. For older adults with pain, the paper advises a balanced approach that includes non-drug approaches, to minimize opioid use.
entries.verifiedAgainst: Table 3, row "Delirium" (opioids; added in 2023 per Table 9)
